text:
Neha: Heads up — I'm doing a 5-city sprint next month (3 conferences + 2 client days). Trying to stay carry-on only. Anyone got go-to sink-laundry / overnight-dry / wrinkle-free outfit rotation tips? Also, do hotels ever actually dry a shirt if you drop it off at 10pm? 😂
Samir: Solid shampoo bars + a packable clothesline saved me. Wring, roll in a towel for 10 min, then hang on the clothesline across the shower — shirts dry by morning if the room is warm and ventilated.
Carmen: +1 for the Sea to Summit travel clothesline. Also carry a few soap sheets (they're paper-thin detergent). For speed, use a hairdryer on cool for a couple minutes after wringing.
Devon: Merino tees = miracle. They resist stink and dry super fast. Roll instead of folding to cut wrinkles. I also pack 1-2 quick-dry undershirts for rotation.
Neha: Any blazer workarounds? Hate hauling a suit bag.
Samir: Hanger-steam trick: hang blazer in bathroom, run shower at the hottest for 5-10 minutes, close door. Steam relaxes wrinkles. If you want better, small handheld steamers (lightweight) are worth the pocket space.
Carmen: If you're at a proper hotel, call the desk: many will do same-day laundry or express pressing if you drop before cutoff (usually ~8am). Late drop-offs sometimes get processed overnight but charge can be steep.
Devon: Shoe tip: rotate two pairs and switch insoles between days so each pair can air out in the shower/bath after arrival. Also put a dryer sheet inside to keep them smelling fresh.
Neha: Is there a tiny travel-size gadget that folds into a hanger or drying rack?
Samir: There's a foldable hanger/dryer thing that clamps to a towel bar. Lightweight and works for socks/underwear.
Carmen: Pack a stain pen and a tiny sewing kit (safety pins + a couple buttons). Also a small zip-lock for wet stuff to keep the rest of the bag dry.
Devon: My packing math: 1 merino tee per day, 1 blazer, 2 bottoms (rotate), undies + socks travel quick-dry. Backup outfit for the last night. Less is more.
ops-bot: Reminder: company travel policy reimburses laundry/dry-cleaning at conferences when required for client-facing events. Save receipts and submit under Travel > Meals & Incidental.
Neha: OMG didn't know we reimburse laundry — life saver, thank you!! :raised_hands: :tada:
Samir: Also pro tip: pack one multipurpose scarf — doubles as warmth on flights, accessory to vary outfits, and can be used as a pillowcase.
Carmen: Quick checklist I use: 
```
- 3x merino tees
- 1 blazer (steamable)
- 2 bottoms (1 casual, 1 dress)
- travel clothesline + soap sheets
- stain pen, safety pin
- small steamer or know the hotel steam trick
- zip-lock for wet items
```
Neha: This is gold. Thanks y'all — packing list assembled. Anyone want to split a small steamer in checked baggage if I end up convinced? :grimacing:
